¤Homology

¤Analogy
  nSimilarity due to convergent evolution
  nAnalogous structureshave the same function in different groups but do not have a common ancestry
  nStructures look similar due to adaptation to similar environments
explanation: Tracing phylogeny involves analyzing different traits. While fossil traits are useful, the fossil record is incomplete, making it difficult to determine the precise evolutionary pathway of a fossil. Systematists distinguish between homology and analogy. Homology refers to biological features that stem from a common ancestor, meaning homologous structures are related through common descent. Analogy refers to structural similarities that arise due to convergent evolution. Analogous structures perform the same function in different groups but do not share a common ancestry; they look similar simply because the unrelated organisms adapted to similar environmental pressures.

opts: Structural similarity due to convergent evolution without common ancestry

questions.exp: Homology refers to traits or structures that are shared among species because they were inherited from a common ancestor.

questions.q: How do analogous structures differ from homologous structures?
opts: Analogous structures have different functions but share a common ancestor.
Analogous structures have the same function in different groups but do not share a common ancestry, arising via convergent evolution.
Analogous structures are only found in prokaryotes.
Analogous structures are determined by Hox genes, while homologous are not.
questions.exp: Analogous structures share similar functions because of adaptation to similar environments (convergent evolution) but lack a common ancestral origin, unlike homologous structures.
